READABILITY.evidence: Names are mostly clear (`buildWindowSpecSql`, `validateWindowName`, `resolvedSpec`). But the WINDOW chunk is one very long line, `sql.join(windows.map((w) => sql`${sql.identifier(w.name)} as (...)`), sql`, `)`, repeated in 5 dialects, and the inline-proxy callback has no comment.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: .window() is not thin as the conventions asked. All 5 select builders copy the same ~20-line body (`typeof spec === 'function' ? spec(new Proxy(this.config.fields, new SelectionProxyHandler(...)))`), and the windowSql builder is duplicated too. The spec logic is shared in window.ts, though.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Window names are checked by validateWindowName (empty and whitespace-only). ntile/nthValue, preceding/following and from/to frame ordering are all validated, tests cover them, and all 130 hidden tests pass. Positional zeros stay inline: `preceding(0)` gives params: [].

C7-01-CASE1.evidence: Purely additive. Each *SelectConfig gets an optional `windows?: WindowDefinition[]`, all five dialects (pg, mysql, sqlite, gel, singlestore) get the same .window(), and SQL only changes when windows are present. No existing signatures changed, and the 566 existing tests still pass.
